prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1487; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling westbound in the left lane when the vehicle drifted across the center line and made contact with an eastbound sedan operated by Driver 2. The impact was head-on but occurred at low speed, and both vehicles came to rest in the travel lanes. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated at the scene; the reported symptoms are consistent with the kind and force of a collision of this nature. Passenger was seated in the front right position of Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed present by both responding officers and by the statements of two independent witnesses, who also observed the vehicles moving as described. Driver 2 stated that the sequence of events matched what was observed at the scene, and photographs taken at the scene show damage concentrated at the front ends of both vehicles, which is largely in line with the described impact. Driver 1 showed no signs of prior damage to the vehicle, and no earlier damage was reported by any party. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy associated with the vehicle. No citations were issued at the time of the report.
